messages:
Maya J.: hey team, first day — quick kubernetes access question. I ran `kubectl config get-contexts` and only see `minikube`. I need access to staging and dev namespaces for my first-week tasks. who do I ping / what info should I include? :wave:

Sam (DevEx): welcome, Maya! :tada: most folks open an infra ticket. Include your corp email, your manager, and the namespaces you need (e.g. `staging`, `dev-maya`). Also paste the output of `kubectl config view --minify --flatten` so we can see what your current kubeconfig looks like.

Maya J.: thanks — pasted output below and opened a ticket but happy to paste here if helpful:
```
apiVersion: v1
clusters: []
contexts: []
current-context: minikube
kind: Config
preferences: {}
users:
- name: minikube
```

I included manager @alex_g and said I need `staging` + `dev-maya`.

onboard-bot: ticket INF-782 created and routed to eng-infra. link: https://tickets.redwood/INF-782

Ira (SRE): hi Maya — quick notes: we do RBAC via group mapping from SSO. You likely need to be added to `redwood-devs` or `redwood-staging-access`. Infra will handle the binding but to speed it up add a short justification in the ticket (what jobs, whether you need write). If you DO need temporary elevated perms, say so and include an expiry date.

Ira (SRE): for the infra team: when you handle this, please check `kubectl auth can-i` after binding. Example I ask the user to run once we add them:
```
kubectl auth can-i get pods --namespace=staging
kubectl get ns
kubectl get pods -n dev-maya
```

Sam (DevEx): adding the onboarding doc link: https://go.redwood/kube-onboard — includes the exact fields we need in the ticket. Quick checklist I copy into tickets: 1) corp email, 2) manager, 3) IRC/Slack handle, 4) namespaces and perms (read/write), 5) duration if temporary, 6) paste `kubectl config view --minify --flatten`.

Maya J.: great, thanks both. I updated INF-782 with the justification and expiry (2 weeks) and requested write on `dev-maya` only.

Ira (SRE): got it, INF-782 looks good. I've queued the rolebinding; you should see access within ~10m. I'll post here when done.

Ira (SRE): done — rolebinding applied. can you run:
```
kubectl auth can-i create deployments --namespace=dev-maya
kubectl get pods -n dev-maya
```

Maya J.: both commands succeeded, I can list pods and create a test deployment. thanks! :raised_hands:

Sam (DevEx): nice — welcome aboard again. If you hit kubeconfig context issues, run `kubectl config use-context <context-name>` or follow the doc. ping me if anything else.
